target_customer: Aerospace, automotive, defense and manufacturing engineering teams needing parts in high performance thermoplastics
problem: Printing advanced thermoplastics such as PEEK and ULTEM required machines costing hundreds of thousands of dollars, or low cost printers that could not handle them.
business_model: Hardware sales of industrial 3D printers plus software, materials support and training

founders.name: Kevin Han
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch Sept 2021: the three met studying materials engineering at McGill.

founders.name: Randeep Singh
founders.background_notes: A 2026 press release names him CEO and co-founder per search summary.

technical_complexity.rationale: Printing PEEK and ULTEM needs heated chambers, hot ends above 400 degrees and materials process knowledge, harder than consumer printers.

defensibility.rationale: Materials process know-how and hardware design help, but other makers such as Intamsys and Apium later sold high temperature machines.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; the company grew independently to 300 plus clients and a 2021 Series A.

market_need_then: The 2021 TechCrunch article describes a gap between machines costing hundreds of thousands of dollars and low cost printers. No 2017 demand data was found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, concise and benefit led; 'Unlocked Materials. Unlocked Applications.'

branding.brand_signature: AON printer line named AON, M2 and M2+, plus Hylo and Basis
branding.community_and_virality: A 2015 Kickstarter raised CAD 89643 for the first printer.

brand_strength.rationale: Known in industrial 3D printing circles and a Kickstarter origin, but no press on the brand itself and the name origin is not given.

pivots.from: 3D printing service bureau and first large format printer
pivots.to: High temperature industrial printers (AON M2) for advanced thermoplastics
pivots.why: Operated printers as a service first and saw a gap for machines handling specialized materials

outcome_analysis: AON3D started with a 2015 Kickstarter and a service bureau, then built high temperature printers for materials like PEEK. It raised an 11.5 million Series A in September 2021 with 14.2 million raised in total and a moon lander partnership with Astrobotic, and a further round in January 2026. It is active with about 40 staff and 300 plus clients.
notes: TechCrunch says total raised was 14.2 million at the Series A, which exceeds the 11.5 million recorded; the remainder (including a seed backed by seven investors per one summary) was not found with a source. The 2026 round amount is not stated. The Kickstarter figure is recorded as a grant stage because it was crowdfunding. Competitor candidates (Intamsys, Apium) came from undated or later sources so none are listed. Han title from YC page; titles for the others conflict.
